descriptions.preferred: The leaves of this selection are the usual shape and size for the species—triangularovate, tapering to a slender tip—but with spectacular variegations. The base color is blue-green. The white to cream and gray-green markings appear on the leaf as specks, flecks, or "cut-in" sections, or sometimes completely covering the leaf. Pink flecks or streaks are often intermixed with the white. Some leaves are entirely white, while others have no variegation. In the fall, the white portions become rose-pink to scarlet. This cultivar forms a tall dense shrub or small tree, reaching 20 ft. (6 m) high. It is named after a famous British nursery which introduced many plants into cultivation. Acer diabolicum Devil maple, horned maple This species is distinguished by curious hornlike stigmas which persist at the inner junction of the fruit nutlets, resembling the horns of the devil. The large, five-lobed, thick-textured leaves are up to 6 in. (15 cm) long. The lobes are divided to about halfway to the leaf base. The middle three lobes are broadly lanceolate-ovate, with short acuminate tips. The two basal lobes are short and small. The margins are irregularly, coarsely, and bluntly toothed. Leaf color is medium to deep green. This strong, medium-sized, sturdy tree reaches 33-50 ft. (10-15 m) tall with a fairly broad, rounded canopy. It can be one of the most spectacular maples in flower, particularly when the bunches of large red male flowers appear. A flowering tree has been described as "looking like the smoldering embers of a gigantic bonfire." This maple is native to Japan, common in the north, less frequent in the south. It is found in open areas on sunny lower mountain slopes from 1320 to 4290 ft. (400-1300 m) above sea level. rhs.description: A large shrub or small, bushy tree to 10m tall and wide with green and white streaked branches and bark. The small, pointed, variegatedleaves are dark green with white and pink mottling in spring and summer and turn pink and purple in autumn. Pale yellow flowers are borne in slender racemes in spring

care.cultivation: Grow in a moist but well-drained soil preferably in full sun
care.propagation: Propagate by grafting or softwood cuttings

resistance.pest: May be susceptible to Acer gall mite, aphids , caterpillars and horse chestnut scale
resistance.disease: May be susceptible to Verticillium wilt , Acer leaf scorch and honey fungus

rhs_zh.description: 大型灌木或小型、丛生状乔木，高和冠幅均可达 10 米。枝条和树皮具绿色与白色条纹。叶片较小、先端尖，具斑锦；春夏季为深绿色，并带白色和粉色斑驳，秋季转为粉色和紫色。春季开淡黄色花，着生于细长总状花序上。

descriptions_zh.preferred: 这一选育品种的叶片形状与大小基本符合本种常态，为三角状卵形，先端渐尖成细长尖头，但具极为醒目的斑锦。底色为蓝绿色。白色至乳白色及灰绿色斑纹可表现为细点、斑块、“切入”状区块，或有时几乎覆盖整片叶。粉色斑点或条纹也常夹杂在白色斑纹之中。有些叶片通体白色，而另一些则完全无斑。秋季时，白色部分会转为玫瑰粉至猩红色。该品种可形成高大而致密的灌木或小乔木，高达 20 英尺（6 米）。其名称取自一家著名的英国苗圃，该苗圃曾将许多植物引入栽培。 Acer diabolicum Devil maple, horned maple 该种可凭借果实小坚果内侧结合处持续宿存的奇特角状柱头而辨认，形似魔鬼之角，因此得名。叶片大型、五裂、质地较厚，长可达 6 英寸（15 厘米）。裂片约分裂至叶基一半处。中间三个裂片为宽披针状卵形，先端短渐尖；基部两裂较短且较小。叶缘具不规则、粗大且钝的锯齿。叶色为中绿至深绿。该树种生长强健，为中等大小且树体结实的乔木，高可达 33-50 英尺（10-15 米），树冠较宽、近圆形。其花期时可成为极为壮观的槭树之一，尤其是大型红色雄花成簇开放时。曾有人形容其开花景象“仿佛一堆巨大篝火尚未熄灭的炽热余烬”。该种原产日本，北部较常见，南部较少见，生于海拔 1320-4290 英尺（400-1300 米）的向阳低山坡开阔地。 Acer distylum 通常称作 Lime-leaved maple。 这一稀有日本种具有极具特征的未裂、心形叶，因此获得这一俗名。分布于本州中北部山区，生于海拔 2275-5200 英尺（700-1600 米）的湿润土壤中。春叶为迷人的浅灰色，并带有浓重的砂色或粉色调，随后夏季转为中绿至深绿，秋季则变为清亮鲜黄。Acer distylum 可长成中等大小乔木，高达 33-49 英尺（10-15 米），是很有观赏价值的园林树种。 Acer japonicum Fullmoon maple 本种的重要特征之一是其绚丽的秋色，黄色、橙色与红色兼具，因此极具园林应用价值。多数类型树势强健，适应多数庭园环境。叶片大型、浓绿色、近圆形，具 9-11 裂。每个裂片较浅，并迅速渐尖。叶缘具浅至粗的锯齿。Acer japonicum 是极具观赏价值的小至中型乔木，高可达 33 英尺（10 米）。原产日本。
